_comment: SN22's deployment settings. Read by kata-subnets-deploy's installer, which validates every
value against its allowlist and ceilings before rendering any unit. This file may set only
what a SUBNET decides for itself.
WHAT CHANGED IN PHASE H, and why each thing is gone:
task_count is 60 and not 8. Upstream deep-scores 20% of a pool and DROPS a contestant with
fewer than three deep samples, so 8 tasks could never be scored at all -- every contestant
would have been zeroed for a reason unrelated to its answers. The plugin refuses any other
value in production rather than rounding it up, because an operator who set one believes
something false about what it will measure.
The data/inference/scrape budgets are GONE. They metered what the VALIDATOR spent on SN22,
and the validator now spends nothing: every paid call happens inside a sealed room with the
contestant's own sealed credentials. A budget for spending that cannot happen is a number
that would only ever mislead whoever read it. The TEE-run and runtime ceilings remain --
those are safety limits on the room, not cost controls on a provider.
KATA_PROMOTE_MARGINS is GONE. It was the indifference band for the seven-signal lexicographic
comparator, which production no longer uses: a duel is decided on one number,
sn22_combined_score, produced by the pinned upstream's own combine_pool_scores over both
contestants' four pool tuples. A margin on that would be Kata overriding upstream's own
arithmetic about what counts as better. A tie keeps the King; strictly greater promotes.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. Five values are required before this lane can run and none of
them is a subnet's to decide -- they change per build and per room:
KATA_SN22_TEE_AGENT_IMAGE      immutable agent image digest (image@sha256:...)
KATA_SN22_TEE_RUNNER_IMAGE     immutable runner image digest
KATA_SN22_ROOM_MEASUREMENT     the only attested room this lane accepts
KATA_SN22_SCORER_POLICY_HASH   what the scores mean
KATA_SN22_ROUTE_POLICY_HASH    which provider routes produced them
The operator supplies them, and kata-subnets-deploy REFUSES to render a unit without all five
(see REQUIRED_OPERATOR_ENV). Putting placeholders here instead would ship a file that looks
configured and is not.

round_gap_sec is 60, the installer's floor -- not a cost decision. It is the idle gap AFTER a round ends, and a round with no pending PR exits in about a second, so this is how long a miner's PR can sit unnoticed. Challenges are timer-driven only: the webhook does intake, screening and queueing, and never starts a duel. At the previous 900 a submission could wait a quarter of an hour with the lane reporting itself healthy and idle.
